summary: Fresh extractions of irCLIP and Pseudo-seq using the same registered cards, papers and diagrams as archived accepted outputs. Authors received revised general instructions, not the earlier extraction or method-specific critiques.
limits: These are selected development cases with one output per harness version, compared with archived baselines. Acceptance is an independent model review, not human validation, wet-lab validation or a general accuracy estimate. The source bytes were held fixed; stochastic variation and other prompt-version differences prevent a causal attribution of every change.

records.name: pseudo_corrected
records.label: Pseudo-seq — first run after automatic correction

findings.title: irCLIP: the starting material is now explicit
findings.finding: The old State identity said “Cellular material containing RNA–protein complexes.” The new identity specifies cells before lysis containing RNA and RNA-binding proteins, and distinguishes the paper’s adherent HeLa preparation from broader catalogue scope. Both graphs have seven Operations, nine States and fifteen Flows.
findings.basis: Same paper:27111506, block b00019; inspect starting State s0 in both saved workflows.

findings.title: A real scientific error was caught and corrected
findings.finding: The first Pseudo-seq author generated treatment and control Operations in a loop. Its control description was correct, but information_effect reused a treatment-specific explanation. The reviewer requested correction of minus_rt; the revision changed only its information_effect and matching attribution-effect statement. No source acquisition or manual artifact rewrite was involved.
findings.basis: paper:25192136, blocks b00003 and b00020; correction_trace retains the author script, first review and exact two-field semantic diff.

findings.title: A conflicting instruction was found in the harness
findings.finding: The shared prompt required separate Operation instances for independent branches while updated reviewer guidance allowed compact independent collections. We aligned those general instructions in a second frozen runtime and repeated only Pseudo-seq. Different routes must remain explicit; equivalent repeated processing may share a block only if condition identity and corresponding products remain recoverable.
findings.basis: runtime_01 versus runtime_02 manifests and prompts; unchanged card and source_registry SHA-256 pins. Fewer nodes alone is not a correctness metric.

findings.title: Pseudo-seq: compact workflow with explicit treatment correspondence
findings.finding: The follow-up author produced eleven Operations, twelve States and twenty-two Flows. Independent review accepted it without a correction. The paired preparations remain separate components; cDNA attribution distinguishes chemical-treatment stops from mock-control background. RNA size-selection order and the analysis description retain their source-supported corrections.
findings.basis: Same card and registry bytes as the baseline. Job 51547846: 143 model review targets accepted. This is a bounded observation; it does not establish that every future compact graph will preserve routing.

findings.title: Clearer prose does not guarantee equally structured assertions
findings.finding: The revised irCLIP extraction describes adapter linkage in prose but no longer uses the baseline’s separate molecular components and typed association properties. Its meaning is readable, but a query that looks only for typed covalent associations would retrieve less. This remains a representation-consistency issue to examine; it is not evidence that the biological linkage disappeared.
findings.basis: Compare baseline States s4/s5 with new s4/s5, including components, properties and their supported prose. No canonical graph was overwritten.
